basic_details.job_title: Chatra North Forest Division Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online for 3 Junior Research Fellow, Senior Research Fellow Posts
basic_details.short_information: The Office of the Divisional Forest Officer, Chatra North Forest Division, Jharkhand, has invited applications for three purely temporary, contractual research posts (1 Senior Research Fellow and 2 Junior Research Fellows) in the Research/Study Team preparing the Working Plan of the division under the National Working Plan Code (NWPC), 2023. The consolidated pay is ₹35,000 per month for the SRF and ₹30,000 per month for the JRF. Candidates need CSIR UGC NET/GATE and a postgraduate degree. content_sections.heading: About Chatra North Forest Division
content_sections.text: The Office of the Divisional Forest Officer, Chatra North Forest Division, is located at Van Bhavan, Chatra (Jharkhand) - 825401. The notice is signed by the Divisional Forest Officer-cum-Working Plan Officer. The research team will prepare the Working Plan of the division in accordance with the National Working Plan Code (NWPC), 2023. This is a government forest department engagement for a project, not a regular post.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The notice lists a tentative 3 posts, and the number of posts may increase or decrease. The notice prints no category-wise break-up of these posts.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Experience: a minimum of two year's research experience, or a candidate pursuing Ph.D. in a relevant discipline. No experience requirement is printed for this post. The notice mentions no desirable qualification. For discipline-specific eligibility, candidates should check the official notification.

rows.essential_qualification: CSIR UGC NET/GATE Qualified. Postgraduate degree (with First Class or 60% marks or equivalent overall grade point average) in Forestry/Ecology/Statistics/Wildlife Biology or allied disciplines.

CSIR UGC NET/GATE Qualified. Postgraduate degree (with First Class or 60% marks or equivalent overall grade point average) in Forestry/Ecology/Botany/Environmental Science/Sociology/Statistics/Watershed Management/Economics or an allied discipline.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The remuneration is consolidated and all-inclusive. No TA/DA, HRA, accommodation, food, medical expenses or any other allowance is admissible. Field travel specifically authorised in writing by the Divisional Forest Officer is reimbursed under applicable departmental norms. The engagement is purely temporary and contractual, coterminous with the project and subject to satisfactory performance. Extension may be considered based on the progress of the Working Plan exercise. It may be terminated at any time for unsatisfactory performance, non-availability of funds or any other administrative reason. It gives no right to regularisation, permanent employment or continuation in service. Activity timelines in the notice run from 2 to 4 months from commencement of each activity. Examples are field enumeration (4 months), biodiversity assessment (4 months), NTFP inventory (3 months) and forest carbon stock assessment (2 months).

content_sections.heading: Chatra North Forest Division Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: The researchers assist in data collection, field surveys, analysis and documentation for the Working Plan. The studies include socio-economic survey, soil survey, biodiversity, NTFP including medicinal and aromatic plants, forest carbon stock, bamboo/rattan, soil erosion and watershed assessment, forest fire impact, wildlife habitat and human-wildlife conflict, and the impact of mining on forest areas. Work is in the interior forest areas of the division and, where required, the peripheral area adjoining the forest boundary for Trees Outside Forests. Overall coordination and supervision of field teams and research activities in accordance with NWPC, 2023. Preparation of study designs, sampling frameworks and data-collection protocols. Analysis and interpretation of field data and preparation of thematic reports under the guidance of the DFO/Working Plan Officer (WPO). Compilation and maintenance of Division-level datasets, including compartment histories, growing-stock data and GIS layers, in the formats prescribed under NWPC, 2023. Maintenance of accurate records, registers and data repositories. Any other work assigned by the DFO(WPO) from time to time. Conduct field surveys and collect data in accordance with approved format under NWPC, 2023. Undertake local community/stake holder interaction for socio-economic and NTFP assessments. Undertake soil sampling, botanical and zoological enumeration and biodiversity documentation. Compile, enter and validate field data. Assist the SRF in preparation of reports, maps and other project outputs/documents. Any other work assigned by the DFO(WPO)/SRF from time to time. The Research Fellows are monitored and supervised by the Working Plan Officer-cum-DFO and submit a fortnightly progress report to the Divisional Forest Officer.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in Chatra North Forest Division Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 3 tentative posts: 1 Senior Research Fellow (SRF) and 2 Junior Research Fellows (JRF). The notice says the number of posts is subject to change.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: Applications must be submitted on or before 10:00 AM on 20 November 2026. No application is entertained after the stipulated date and time.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for SRF and JRF?
faq.answer: Both posts need CSIR UGC NET/GATE and a postgraduate degree with First Class or 60% marks in the listed disciplines or allied ones. The SRF also needs two years' research experience, or must be pursuing a Ph.D. in a relevant discipline.

faq.question: Q4. What is the salary of SRF and JRF at Chatra North Forest Division?
faq.answer: The SRF gets a consolidated ₹35,000 per month and the JRF ₹30,000 per month. The remuneration is all-inclusive, with no TA/DA, HRA or other allowance.

faq.question: Q5. How can I apply?
faq.answer: Email your CV, scanned certificates, email ID and mobile number to [email protected] or [email protected], stating the post applied for. You can also post the application in the Annexure-A pro forma to the Chatra office at Van Bhavan, Chatra (Jharkhand) 825401.

faq.question: Q6. When and where is the walk-in interview?
faq.answer: The Walk-in Interview is on 20 November 2026 at 11:00 AM at the Office of the Divisional Forest Officer, Chatra North Forest Division, Van Bhavan, Chatra (Jharkhand) 825401.

faq.question: Q7. What should I carry to the interview?
faq.answer: Carry original certificates, mark-sheets and experience certificates, one set of self-attested photocopies, a recent passport-size photograph and a valid photo identity document, along with the filled application form.

faq.question: Q8. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. The engagement is purely temporary and contractual, coterminous with the project. It gives no right to regularisation, permanent employment or continuation in service, though an extension may be considered based on progress.

faq.question: Q9. Is travel allowance paid for attending the interview?
faq.answer: No TA/DA is admissible for attending the Walk-in Interview. Field travel specifically authorised in writing by the Divisional Forest Officer is reimbursed under departmental norms.

faq.question: Q10. How much notice is needed to leave or end the engagement?
faq.answer: A selected candidate who wants to leave must give at least 15 days' prior written notice. The Divisional Forest Officer may terminate the engagement on one week's prior notice if timelines or responsibilities are not met.
